verdict_label: Better to use an open hand
explanation: The conventional way to beckon someone in Spain is palm-up with a scooping wave of the fingers or whole hand, not a single curled index finger. Using the curled-finger version isn't a dramatic insult the way it is in places like the Philippines, but it can read as brusque or over-familiar, particularly toward someone older or a stranger, so the open-hand version is the safer, more natural choice.
local_tip: Beckon with your palm up and fingers (or whole hand) curling toward you, rather than a single crooked index finger.

also_check.note: Beckoning with a single finger is considered impolite and is associated with calling animals; a palm-down wave is used instead.
This gesture is strongly associated with calling dogs and is considered a serious insult when directed at a person.
It's less charged than in some other cultures, but can still come across as overly familiar or dismissive rather than a polite way to call someone over.
